description: Verify that DUT silently discards an IPv4 UDP packet whose Destination Address is a Directed Broadcast (subnet broadcast like 192.168.0.255) — directed broadcasts must not be accepted by hosts on the destination subnet (RFC 1122 §3.2.1.3 SHOULD NOT receive)
approach:
[Objective]
Directed broadcast = the subnet broadcast for some other subnet (e.g. 192.168.0.255 reaches every host in 192.168.0.0/24). For TC8 / RFC 1122 §3.2.1.3, hosts SHOULD NOT receive directed broadcasts addressed to their subnet — too easy to abuse for amplification attacks. DUT must drop.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 UDP packet
   • dst_ip = directed broadcast for DUT's subnet
   • dst_port = a port DUT's upper-tester listens on

2. Observation:
   • Upper-tester does NOT see the UDP datagram

[Pass condition]
DUT did not deliver the datagram to its upper-tester.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_receipt — DUT delivered the datagram (RFC 1122 SHOULD NOT violation)
• Fail_timeout — handshake/observation timed out indeterminately

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the directed-broadcast UDP — normal
verdicts.Fail_wrong_receipt: DUT delivered the directed-broadcast UDP — RFC 1122 SHOULD NOT violation
verdicts.Fail_timeout: Observation timed out without a clear verdict
